observation.visible_scene: A wide, calm pond or lake viewed from a fixed shore-side position. Floating lily pads are scattered across the water, with a denser cluster in the lower-middle of the frame. A line of stepping stones / a low floating barrier runs diagonally along the left side of the water. The far shore is lined with dense green trees and low hills, and a dark, angular roofed structure sits at the center of the treeline. The upper half of the frame is a bright blue sky filled with white cumulus clouds. A cursive watermark ('Homedar Liu') is fixed in the bottom-right corner throughout.
visible_changes: The background (hills, trees, building, sky, clouds, watermark, stepping-stone line) holds the same pixel positions from the first to the last frame, so the camera is stationary and there is no scene translation.

The only continuous motion is on the water surface: concentric ripple rings centered on the lower-middle lily-pad cluster persist and subtly reshape from frame to frame, indicating an ongoing wave disturbance already present at t=0 and continuing past t=2.67s.
The milky cloud reflections on the left and center water shimmer and break apart slightly as the ripples pass, but the reflected cloud shapes themselves do not drift.
The lily pads remain in essentially the same locations across the excerpt, with only faint bobbing tied to the passing ripples rather than any net drift.
A darker submerged patch near the center of the pond stays roughly constant in position and extent.
outside_clip_unknowns: What produced the ripples (a fish, a falling object, wind, or a current) is not visible within the segment.
Whether the ripple source was active before the crop or stops after it is unknown; the rings are already expanding at the first frame and still present at the last.
uncertain_details: The exact center/origin of the ripple pattern is hard to pin down because the rings overlap the lily pads.
It is unclear whether the small ring set in the right-center water is a second disturbance or a continuation of the same wave field.
Any very slow cloud drift is below the resolution of this 2.67s excerpt and cannot be confirmed.
